title: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף

paragraphs: Rav Acha, son of Rav Yosef, spoke to Rav Chisda, Chullin 105a; Bava Metzia 87a. He spoke to Rav Ashi, Yevamot 31b; Menachot 35b. He challenged Rav Ashi, who said, “When you reach Shechitat Kodashim, challenge me.” Rashi: “I recognized your sharpness,” Bava Metzia 109b. Rav Ashi sat considering, etc.; Rav Mordekhai told him, “Thus said Avimi of Hagrunya in Rava’s name,” etc. Rav Acha bar Rav Yosef told Rav Ashi, “But we say in Rava’s name,” Bava Metzia 77, end of b. He said in Mar Zutra’s name in Rav Pappa’s name, Chullin 43a. He fell ill with jaundice; Rav Kahana cured him, Shemonah Sheratzim 110b—apparently the later Rav Kahana. Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef thought to say before Rav Yosef, Eruvin 29b. But how could a man in Rav Ashi’s days have spoken to Rav Chisda and Rav Yosef, presumably as an adult? Rav Chisda died before Rava (see there), and Rav Ashi was born when Rava died.
